author: Declaration Desk
title: Aditya-L1 data show a 2024 solar eruption expanded unevenly, not as a symmetric bubble
dek: Indian Institute of Astrophysics scientists combined the coronagraph's readings with NASA imagery; the finding bears on space-weather forecasting.
body:
Scientists at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Bengaluru, have reported that a coronal mass ejection (CME) seen on 5 August 2024 expanded unevenly rather than as a symmetric bubble, using data from India's Aditya-L1 solar mission. The study was published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters on 3 November 2026, according to GKToday's summary; we have not read the paper itself.

The team combined readings from Aditya-L1's Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) with images from NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory and three-dimensional modelling. VELC's spectroscopy of the Fe XIV 5303 Å coronal line measured line-of-sight plasma velocities of up to 218 km/s, a projected radial speed of 1,135 km/s and a lateral speed in the plane of the sky of 692 km/s, GKToday reported.

Why it matters: how a CME expands can change its speed and its path towards Earth, and so how it affects satellites and power grids. Models that assume a symmetric bubble may therefore misjudge arrival and impact. GKToday said earlier VELC results this month included a joint analysis with the European Proba-3 mission, published on 15 October.

sources.title: GKToday: Aditya-L1 Detects Asymmetric Expansion of Solar Eruption
